::: {.keyidea}
[Thesis]{.k-title}
This is **step 3 of the uncertainty arc** — the culmination of the arc, and the
least reproducible quantity in the discipline. A depth profile of velocity change
[from step 2](theory-processing-depth.qmd) becomes effective stress and strain
only through a **petrophysical model**, and the coefficients that model requires
are poorly constrained — so the stress uncertainty is dominated by *epistemic*
prior uncertainty, not by the measurement. This page is a **framework**: the physics
and the honest budget are set out here, and the executable modules
(`uq_stress_depth`, `uq_attribution`) are tracked as open development. The
[companion inference-UQ page](theory-uq.qmd) holds the Bayesian
stress-inversion machinery this step draws on.
:::

## Where the field stands

The quantity of interest is rarely the velocity change itself but the stress,
strain, or pore-pressure change that produces it and — increasingly — the forcing
responsible for it. Here the literature remains fragmented. Volcano and fault
studies often interpret the velocity change qualitatively (a pre-eruptive
pressurization, coseismic damage); hydrological studies fit an explicit
poroelastic or thermoelastic model and separate the two by their seasonal phase
lag (Tsai 2011; Wang 2017; Clements & Denolle 2018); and a growing body quantifies
stress sensitivity through an acoustoelastic coefficient (Brenguier et al. 2008;
Nakata & Snieder 2011). What is largely absent is the *uncertainty* on that final
quantity and a defensible apportionment of it among the competing forcings.

## From velocity change to effective stress

Effective stress follows from strain through the elastic moduli, and strain
follows from the velocity change through the acoustoelastic **bridge relation**

$$
\beta(z) = -\frac{\mu'(z)\,\kappa(z)}{2\,\mu(z)} \qquad\text{(Denolle, in prep., Eq. 7)},
$$

with $\mu(z)=\rho V_S^2$ and $\kappa(z)=\rho\,(V_P^2-\tfrac43 V_S^2)$ read from a
velocity model. Per depth, the volumetric strain is
$\varepsilon_{\rm vol}(z)=(\delta V_S/V_S)(z)/\beta(z)$ and the effective-stress
change is $\Delta\sigma'(z)=\kappa(z)\,\varepsilon_{\rm vol}(z)$. Total stress adds
a poroelastic term $\alpha_B(z)\,\Delta p(z)$ and is carried as an **optional
extension**, since effective stress is what $\delta v/v$ most directly senses and
is poroelastically clean.

The coefficients $\beta(z),\mu'(z)$ are **layered** and weakly constrained —
sometimes inferred from a tomographic $V_P,V_S$ model — so they enter as
**per-layer priors**. The honest stress covariance is the Monte-Carlo pushforward
of the depth posterior $C_m(z)$ *through* those priors. This is the step where the
aleatoric measurement chain and the epistemic material priors **merge**; taking
either alone understates the stress uncertainty. It is the depth-resolved analogue
of the scalar pushforward already shown in
[tutorial 5](tutorial-05-interpretation.qmd).

## Attribution: which forcing, and with what confidence

Beyond the *state* of stress, the community wants **attribution**: how much of the
change at depth $z$ is poroelastic, thermoelastic, load, damage, or tectonic, and
with what confidence. The natural frame is the geophysical analogue of climate
detection-and-attribution — **optimal fingerprinting** scaled by the very
measurement covariance $C_d$ this arc builds.

- **Apportionment.** Each forcing $k$ predicts a depth–time effective-stress
  fingerprint; a generalized-least-squares regression weighted by $C_d$ gives its
  amplitude, and a variance decomposition gives its share $A_k(z)$ of the stress
  variability at each depth. The cross-covariances quantify how ambiguous the
  attribution is when two forcings are collinear (thermoelastic and hydrologic are
  both seasonal).
- **Coupling.** When forcings couple, the additive decomposition gives way to
  **Sobol** variance indices whose interaction term *is* the coupling
  contribution — the [coupling framework](theory-uq.qmd) expressed as an
  attribution component.
- **Confidence.** Sampling the joint posterior — forcing amplitudes, material
  priors, and the measurement realization — turns each share into a credible
  interval and, decomposed further, indicates whether a weak attribution is
  **data-limited or model-limited** — i.e., which additional data would most
  reduce it.

The deliverable is a depth–source attribution chart — per depth, a stacked bar of
$A_k(z)$ with credible-interval whiskers plus an explicit coupling slice
("at 200 m: 60% poroelastic ±15%, 25% thermoelastic ±10%, 10% co-seismic,
5% coupling").

## Best practice versus deviation

| Choice | Best practice | Common deviation | Consequence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Stress conversion | Acoustoelastic bridge with layered $\beta(z),\mu'(z)$ priors | Single scalar coefficient, no prior | Understated (epistemic) stress error |
| Uncertainty budget | Merge the aleatoric depth covariance with the epistemic material priors | Report the measurement error only | Stress error too small by its dominant term |
| Stress measure | Report effective stress; flag any total-stress assumptions | Conflate effective and total stress | Non-comparable, ambiguous stress |
| Forcing separation | Physical diagnostic (seasonal phase lag, branch, coupling test) | Attribute by eye | Mis-attribution when forcings are collinear |
| Attribution uncertainty | Credible intervals plus a data- vs model-limited split | A single point attribution | No measure of confidence, nor of which data would most reduce it |

::: {.callout-note}
## Status — framework, implementation in progress
This page is the design for step 3. The executable modules — a depth-resolved
`uq_stress_depth` (strain, effective stress, and their covariance from a
$\delta V_S/V_S(z)$ posterior and layered petrophysical priors) and a
`uq_attribution` module (optimal-fingerprinting shares, Sobol indices, detection,
and the data- vs model-limited budget) — are tracked in the repository issues.
Their inputs are a real $C_d$ (step 1) and an honest depth posterior (step 2),
which is why the whole arc has to be built in order.
:::
